apps.name: Parallel Search
apps.tagline: Public-web search and source extraction, free for light use.
apps.description: Searches the public web and pulls the passages that answer a question, with the sources they came from. The anonymous endpoint is rate-limited and takes no key; add the API-key entry instead when a bot needs to search a lot.
apps.creator: Parallel

prompts.text: Search the public web for what changed in this release and summarize each source.
Extract the concrete numbers from these pages, with the URL each came from.

apps.name: Parallel Search (API key)
apps.tagline: Public-web search and extraction on this computer's Parallel API key.
apps.description: The same search and extraction as the anonymous entry, authenticated with a Parallel API key so a bot is not held to the free rate limit. The key stays on this computer and is sent as a bearer token.
apps.creator: Parallel

fields.label: Parallel API key
fields.hint: From the Parallel platform. Saved on this computer only.

prompts.text: Build a sourced brief on this question; keep every claim next to its URL.

apps.name: Exa Search
apps.tagline: Semantic public-web search and page reading, rate-limited without a key.
apps.description: Finds pages by meaning rather than keywords and reads them back, which suits questions a literal search misses. The anonymous endpoint is rate-limited; the API-key entry removes that limit.
apps.creator: Exa

prompts.text: Find pages that argue the opposite of this article and list them.
Read these links and list what each one claims, with quotes.

apps.name: Exa Search (API key)
apps.tagline: Semantic public-web search on this computer's Exa API key.
apps.description: The same search and reading as the anonymous entry, authenticated with an Exa API key. Exa reads its key from an x-api-key header rather than an Authorization bearer, so the key is sent that way.
apps.creator: Exa

fields.label: Exa API key
fields.hint: From the Exa dashboard. Saved on this computer only.

prompts.text: Search deeply for primary sources on this, then read the three best.

apps.name: Firecrawl
apps.tagline: Public-web search, scraping and crawling, free for search and scrape.
apps.description: Searches, scrapes and maps public sites and turns pages into clean text a bot can work from. Crawls, agents and browser sessions start work at Firecrawl, which the reviewed write list covers; search, scrape and map only read.
apps.creator: Firecrawl

prompts.text: Scrape this page and list its release dates with links.
Map this documentation site and name the pages about authentication.

apps.name: Firecrawl (API key)
apps.tagline: Public-web scraping on this computer's Firecrawl API key.
apps.description: The same search, scraping and crawling as the anonymous entry, authenticated with a Firecrawl API key for higher limits and the write tools the free tier restricts. The key stays on this computer and is sent as a bearer token.
apps.creator: Firecrawl

fields.label: Firecrawl API key
fields.hint: From the Firecrawl dashboard. Saved on this computer only.

prompts.text: Crawl this changelog and summarize every entry from the last release.

apps.name: Google Drive
apps.tagline: Files and documents in the Drive of whoever is asking.
apps.description: Searches, lists and reads the Drive of the signed-in person, so two people asking the same question get the answers their own accounts can see. Read-only: Docs, Sheets and Slides are exported as text, and nothing writes back. Google's MCP server is behind the Workspace Developer Preview Program, so a Google Cloud project must be enrolled before the connector answers.
apps.creator: Google

fields.label: OAuth client ID
fields.hint: Google issues no pasted token: this app signs each person in, so it needs a client of yours. Create an OAuth client (type Web application) in Google Cloud console → APIs & Services → Credentials, enable the Drive API on the project, and add both redirect addresses from Codync's guide as allowed redirect URIs.

fields.label: OAuth client secret
fields.hint: The client secret that goes with the ID. Saved on this computer only.

prompts.text: Find the document about the launch plan and summarize its decisions.
Which of my files changed this week, and what are they about?

apps.name: Notion
apps.tagline: Pages and databases of whoever is asking.
apps.description: Searches, fetches and queries the Notion pages and databases the signed-in person shares, and can create or update pages when asked. Access is chosen page by page on Notion's own consent screen: there is no read-only scope, so the reviewed write list is the barrier. Each connection registers Codync with Notion itself, so there is nothing to paste.
apps.creator: Notion

prompts.text: Search Notion for the onboarding page and list what it still leaves open.
Query this quarter's project database and group the items by owner.

apps.name: Routines
apps.tagline: Standing instructions a bot runs on a schedule.
apps.description: Codync's own routines, offered to bots as tools the same way a connector's tools are: create, update, pause and delete routines, their triggers and their goals. First-party and always on, so there is nothing to install and no key to hold. Codync keeps them in its own schedule, so a routine also runs while nobody is chatting.
apps.creator: OpenBot

prompts.text: Make a routine that every Friday at 16:00 lists what slipped this week.
